The get_config response only includes cloudhook_url/remote_ui_url when there is an active subscription, so once the user logs out the iOS app never learns the cloudhook is gone and keeps posting to hooks.nabu.casa; it should explicitly signal removal (e.g. return None or omit with clearing semantics).

The cloud config entry created via the system flow persists after logout/removal of default_config, so the integration and its 3 entities stay loaded; the entry should be removed on logout or when cloud is not configured.
Logout does not remove the cloud config entry or its cloudhooks, leaving the integration and stale webhook state behind.
Cloudhook cleanup is only done on entry data and doesn't notify the companion app that the stored cloudhook URL is no longer valid.

files.lines: async_setup_entry, lines ~75-118 (address lookup and the 'no known LAN address yet' skip at ~100-106)
files.why: Devices without an address learned via DHCP are skipped with no coordinator or entities, because the integration relies solely on DHCP discovery, which never fires for already-leased devices. Setup needs its own way to resolve the LAN IP (for example the cloud-provided address, or an active lookup by MAC), and it should not slow setup or fail it with a timeout.
The user step creates the entry without any LAN address discovery, and the DHCP step is the only source of IPs, so the entry starts with an empty CONF_ADDRESSES and devices never get set up.
DHCP matching on registered devices is the only discovery mechanism and doesn't find devices that already hold leases; it needs a supplement or replacement (such as a hostname or MAC-prefix matcher).

files.lines: catch_request_errors decorator (lines ~65-87, the except UpnpError at line 82-85); the 12 action handlers with `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` (lines ~615-845)
files.why: The shared decorator wrapping all the action handlers catches UpnpError and only logs it, so it must raise HomeAssistantError (with translation_domain/key) and the pylint disable comments must be removed.
The new HomeAssistantError translation keys used by the handlers need their messages defined here.
The call never passes a notify_self option, so messages the account sends to its own number arrive silently. It should pass notify_self=True, or set it when a recipient equals the sender number.

If pysignalclirestapi 0.3.25 has no notify_self parameter on send_message, the pin must be bumped to a release that has one. requirements_all.txt and requirements_test_all.txt must be regenerated to match.
Non-Input sensors (e.g. Output type) get no unique ID but still return device_info, so either give every sensor a unique ID or return device_info only when _attr_unique_id is set.
The device identifier and serial number are built from the prefixed external-device key, so the identifier no longer matches the original plain-serial device and a second, empty device is created.

files.lines: OpenGarageCover class (is_closing/is_opening, async_close_cover/async_open_cover, _update_attr); add an async_toggle override or current_cover_position (100 when open)
files.why: The entity reports transient CLOSING, which flips the base class's _cover_is_last_toggle_direction_open to False. A later toggle on the now-open door then calls async_open_cover, which returns early because the state is already OPEN, so nothing happens.
For a cover without position reporting, the stale last-direction flag decides the toggle even when is_closed is False, so a known-open door can be toggled in the wrong direction.

Both iterate over all DOMAIN config entries and read runtime_data, which doesn't exist on entries that are not loaded (setup failed/retrying/disabled), raising AttributeError; they should filter to entries with state ConfigEntryState.LOADED (or use async_loaded_entries).
The handler only logs the RequestException; it must raise HomeAssistantError (with translation_domain/key) from err and drop the pylint disable comment.
A translation key for the new HomeAssistantError (e.g. failed to communicate with IFTTT) must be defined.

files.lines: XboxPresenceCoordinator.update_data, lines ~216-219 (get_friend_by_xuid for own profile / get_friends_own)
files.why: The `detail.has_game_pass` flag on the Person objects returned by the people endpoints doesn't reflect the account's real Game Pass (Ultimate) subscription, so the coordinator needs to fetch the subscription status from a reliable source (e.g. the profile or subscription API) and store it in the presence data.
The sensor reads `x.detail.has_game_pass` straight from the Person model, so it must be changed to use the corrected Game Pass data.

files.lines: async_send_message / send_message, lines ~85-100 (OSError except at 92-96 and the 'Path is not whitelisted' branch); also line 121 uses str(err)
files.why: The OSError handler only logs (with the pylint disable comment) so it must raise HomeAssistantError with translation_domain/key and the disable comment removed.
It needs the new translation keys (e.g. attachment read failure, path not whitelisted) used by the raised HomeAssistantError.
The low_battery binary sensor is driven by the sticky 'Low Battery' notification via FlumeNotificationBinarySensor.is_on, and should instead be derived from the device's current battery level.
It only keeps the 'connected' flag from the device list, so it must also store the current battery level from the device data for the battery sensor to use.
This constant becomes unused once the battery sensor stops using notifications, and a battery-level key and low-battery threshold may need to be added.
The dict lacks the "attisPro" model number (e.g. add "attisPro": "ecobee Smart Thermostat Pro"), which triggers the 'Unrecognized model number' warning in climate.py.

For multi-mode bulbs (e.g. RGBWW + COLOR_TEMP), _attr_color_mode stays None whenever the state reports neither a color temp nor RGBWW/RGBW values, so state_attributes raises "does not report a color mode"; it needs a fallback to a valid supported mode (and the scene branch should only set BRIGHTNESS/ONOFF if supported).

The subscription is retried only when it raises a TraccarException; when the websocket closes normally or drops, subscribe() returns, the background task ends and no updates arrive, so it needs a reconnect loop that resubscribes after any disconnect (and ideally refreshes data).
The subscription runs once as a background task with no supervision or restart, so it should be restarted when it ends.

The pinned pyanglianwater library's MSOB2C login no longer works against Anglian Water's current login flow, so it needs a bump to a fixed release.
Generated requirements must match the bumped version in manifest.json.
Test requirements must match the bumped version in manifest.json.
The new library may raise different exceptions, so the flow may need to map them correctly instead of reporting every failure as invalid_auth.

files.lines: async_step_init, the vol.Optional(CONF_LLM_HASS_API, default=...) schema entry (~lines 242-250), plus the user_input pop at ~183-184
files.why: The field uses default=self.options.get(CONF_LLM_HASS_API, [Assist]). When the user unchecks everything, the empty value is dropped and voluptuous restores the Assist default on submit. The key is also popped when saved, so the form falls back to the Assist default on reopen. It should use description={"suggested_value": self.options.get(CONF_LLM_HASS_API)} with no default, which is the pattern other LLM integrations use.
It calls async_extract_entity_ids(service) with the default expand_group=True, so group.* ids are replaced by their members; pass expand_group=False so the group's own entity_id is purged.

Aux properties (CPW/TPW power and energy controls etc.) are only turned into sensors for Insteon nodes, so Z-Wave nodes such as a power-monitoring plug never get sensors; the protocol check must also cover Z-Wave (PROTO_ZWAVE).
Aux sensors from Z-Wave nodes need the right device class, state class and unit mapping for the power and energy controls, and the aux sensor needs to handle the Z-Wave control/uom values.

files.lines: HomeConnectSensor.async_added_to_hass and fetch_unit (~lines 654-674); description at ~189-193 (COOKING_OVEN_CURRENT_CAVITY_TEMPERATURE, fetch_unit=True)
files.why: The temperature unit is only set when the entity is added and only if the API returns a unit, so when the status has no unit and the fetch fails or returns none, the sensor reports no unit (''). The sensor needs a stable unit (for example a fixed or fallback unit, or one persisted and kept) instead of flapping between '' and °F.

The group only sends a shutter level, with no slats level. The group's default slats value (0, open) is then applied after the shutters close, so the group close should also set the slats level to closed (HMIP_SLATS_CLOSED), or the slats value should be passed through when the group moves.

files.lines: EnvoyConsumptionEntity.native_value (~1189-1200), plus the daily_consumption description in CONSUMPTION_SENSORS (~291-300). Same for EnvoyConsumptionPhaseEntity (~1239), the net-consumption entities (~1203, ~1261) and the per-phase copies of the sensors.
files.why: The daily consumption value (watt_hours_today) is published unfiltered as a TOTAL_INCREASING sensor, so a uint32-max sentinel (~2^32 Wh) must be rejected here (return None/unavailable, or drop the update) before it reaches the state machine and recorder.

The radon sensor uses a plain "Bq/m³" string with no device_class, so the sensor framework can't offer unit conversion; it needs device_class=SensorDeviceClass.RADON and native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfRadiationConcentration.BECQUERELS_PER_CUBIC_METER so users can pick pCi/L.

A non-root endpoint that is not flagged as a bridged device gets the same MatterNodeDevice identifier as the bridge root endpoint, so the AC and the bridge collapse into one device.
The via_device link and the bridge detection depend on is_bridged_device, so an Aqara AC endpoint that is not flagged as bridged is merged with the bridge and becomes its own parent.
The entity DeviceInfo uses the same identifier, so it must follow the corrected device ID to attach AC entities to the AC device rather than the bridge device.

files.lines: calc_derivative(), the total_increasing negative-derivative branch (~lines 540-553); also the on_state_reported zero short-circuit (~442) and _last_valid_state_time handling
files.why: When the cumulative source returns from unavailable at midnight with 0, the delta against the stale pre-midnight value is negative, so the sample is dropped by an early return that neither updates _last_valid_state_time to the new 0 baseline nor writes a state, leaving the derivative unavailable until a second valid sample arrives.

files.lines: async_setup_entry (async_add_entities([entity], True)); RemoteCalendarEntity._async_update_timeline / _get_timeline (materialize_timeline with MAX_LOOKAHEAD_TIME / MAX_LOOKAHEAD_EVENTS); event property
files.why: The log shows the entity state update taking 91 s on the event loop. Entity setup and timeline materialization for a huge calendar are CPU-heavy and starve the loop, so the update should not run before add and the materialization should be bounded or kept off the loop.
Parsing a large ICS runs in an executor thread but is CPU-bound and holds the GIL, which can freeze HA. It may need to be made cheaper or made to yield.

files.lines: MieleSuperSwitch.is_on (~line 223-230) and the supercooling/superfreezing entries in SWITCH_TYPES (~lines 54-79)
files.why: is_on is true only when state_status equals exactly on_value (14 or 13), so any other status the device reports while super-cooling or super-freezing, for example 146 (supercooling_superfreezing) or a different status reported by freezers, leaves the switch off.
The enum has missing_to_none=True, so a status code it doesn't list is read as None. A missing code would also leave the switch off, so the enum may need an extra member.
